strings.app.title: Battery Monitor
strings.app.subtitle: Real-Time Battery Dashboard
strings.rt.title: Real-Time Monitor
strings.hist.title: Charge History
strings.hist.empty_hint: Charge your Mac then tap Refresh
strings.proc.title: Power-Hungry Processes
strings.tip.charge_power: Real-time power (W) flowing into or out of the battery. Positive = charging, negative = discharging.
strings.tip.adapter: Rated wattage of the connected power adapter. 0W means no adapter detected.
strings.tip.temperature: Current battery cell temperature. Normal range: 20–35°C. Above 40°C may throttle performance.
strings.tip.cycles: Total charge cycles consumed. Apple rates batteries for ~1000 cycles before health drops below 80%.
strings.tip.health: Current max capacity vs. original design capacity. 100% = brand new. Below 80% = consider replacement.
strings.tip.condition: System-assessed battery condition based on health metrics and cycle count.
strings.tip.voltage: Battery terminal voltage. Typical range: 10–13V for MacBook batteries.
strings.tip.amperage: Charge/discharge current in milliamps. Positive = charging, negative = discharging.
strings.tip.power: Instantaneous power = |Current| × Voltage. Shows real-time energy flow.
strings.tip.percent: Current state of charge as percentage of usable capacity.
strings.tip.charge_rate: How many percent the battery gains per hour. Higher = faster charging.
strings.tip.cpu: CPU usage percentage of this process. Higher CPU = more power draw.
strings.insight.headline.excellent: Your battery is in excellent shape — every indicator is in the ideal range.
strings.insight.headline.good: Your battery is in good shape. Keep up your current habits.
strings.insight.headline.good_high_cycle: Well cared for despite %d charge cycles — still in good shape.
strings.insight.headline.fair_capacity: Capacity has dropped to %.0f%%. No noticeable impact day to day, but worth watching.
strings.insight.headline.fair_resistance: Internal resistance is rising. Avoid heavy use while charging in hot conditions.
strings.insight.headline.poor: The battery has aged noticeably. Runtime is likely shorter — plan a replacement.
strings.insight.headline.critical: Battery health is critically low. Contact Apple Support soon.
strings.insight.factor.fault_found: Fault flag set — have it checked
strings.insight.life.label: Remaining life
strings.insight.age.label: Battery age
strings.insight.age.tip: Estimated from charge cycles and an assumed ~1.3 cycles per day. Not the actual manufacture date — Apple Silicon does not expose one.
strings.insight.habit.tip_optimized_charging: Turn on Optimized Battery Charging in System Settings → Battery. macOS will learn your routine and hold off on the last 20%%.
strings.insight.habit.tip_avoid_overnight: You often leave it plugged in at 100%% overnight. Charging to about 80%% before bed is gentler on the battery.
strings.insight.habit.tip_full_cycle: Try to stay between 20%% and 80%%. Running down to empty is the hardest on a battery.
strings.insight.habit.tip_temp: Battery reached %d°C while charging. Remove thick cases or move somewhere cooler.
strings.insight.accessory.disconnected_hint: Plug in to run the accessory check
strings.insight.accessory.tip_low_power: This charger delivers %dW but the Mac can take %dW. A higher-rated charger would charge faster.
strings.insight.accessory.tip_negotiation: The charger did not negotiate a voltage. Try another cable or port.
strings.insight.power.note_top: Drawing %.1fW right now. “%@” is the biggest CPU consumer at %.0f%% — closing it should help.
strings.insight.habit.shallow_none: No short top-ups logged this week
strings.insight.factor.capacity_note: Same definition as System Settings. The raw cell ratio is lower because Apple accounts for the reserve buffer.
strings.hw.rel.derived: Computed by us, not from registry
strings.hw.n.weighted_ra: Apple does not publish an acceptable range. The trend over time is reliable; a single absolute value is not.
strings.hw.n.qmax: Chemical capacity per cell, learned between two open-circuit-voltage anchors. Cells are in series, so pack capacity is the weakest cell, not the sum.
strings.hw.n.cell_voltage: Cells are in series: voltages add, capacity does not. Their sum equals the pack voltage.
strings.hw.n.design_cycles: Use this as the basis for remaining life. Extrapolating current capacity fade linearly badly overestimates degradation during break-in.
strings.hw.n.raw_max: Full-charge capacity learned by the gauge (equals FccComp1/2). Not the chemical total — the unusable portion has already been subtracted.
strings.hw.n.raw_current: Not measured directly — computed as FCC × (1 − depth of discharge), where DOD comes from coulomb counting corrected by open-circuit voltage.
strings.hw.n.reserve: Buffer never exposed to the user. Apple adds it back to the numerator and subtracts it from the denominator — that is why System Settings shows a higher health figure than the raw ratio.
strings.hw.n.temp_unit: Scale differs by platform: Apple Silicon reports centi-°C, some Intel Macs report deci-°C. We decide by magnitude.
strings.hw.n.temp_avg: Note the mixed scales: within the same dictionary, Average is deci-°C while Min/Max are plain °C.
strings.hw.n.system_power: Already in watts, and it stays live on battery — the preferred source for power analysis.
strings.hw.n.charge_i_limit: Zero also appears when the battery is full and holding, or right after plugging in — it does not by itself mean charging is being throttled.
strings.hw.n.not_charging_reason: Bit meanings are undocumented, so we show the raw value and draw no conclusion from it.
strings.hw.n.ac_only: Instantaneous telemetry reads zero on battery power — this row only appears while plugged in.
strings.hw.n.total_runtime: Semantics unclear: far too low to be wall-clock age on this machine, so we do not use it to infer battery age.
strings.hw.n.max_discharge: Already a signed negative integer — no two's-complement conversion needed.
strings.hw.n.min_pack_voltage: The lowest pack voltage ever reached — empirical anchor for where the cutoff actually lies.
strings.hw.n.daily_soc: Today's snapshot only — the gauge keeps no history, so weekly figures must be accumulated by this app.
strings.hw.n.health_system: Matches System Settings. Formula reverse-engineered as (FCC + reserve) / (design − reserve); verified on one machine only.
strings.hw.n.health_raw: Plain physical ratio with no reserve adjustment. Lower than the figure System Settings shows — both are correct under different definitions.
strings.hw.n.unusable: Computed by the gauge itself, not estimated by us: it uses the impedance table to find where terminal voltage would fall below cutoff, and excludes that charge.
strings.hw.n.deficit_cycle: Describes what has already happened. Do NOT extrapolate it: lithium-ion fade is fast early then flattens, so a linear projection gives an absurdly short life.
strings.hw.n.deficit_total: Charge permanently consumed by side reactions (SEI film growth). It never passes through the sense resistor, so coulomb counting cannot see it — only relearning Qmax reveals it.
strings.hw.n.calib_age: The gauge can only relearn capacity when the pack rests long enough to read open-circuit voltage. Staying plugged in keeps this number growing and the health reading stale.
strings.hw.n.topology: nSmP means n cells in series, m in parallel. In series, voltages add but capacity does not — the pack is limited by the weakest cell.
